subject: Re: Urgent: suspected ingestion anomaly — preliminary notice & request for forensic snapshot
messages:
From: Alex Gupta <alex.gupta@asteronlabs.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@asteronlabs.com>
Date: 2028-01-15T08:04:00-05:00
Subject: Suspected ingestion anomaly — initial heads up

Hi Kimberly,

We detected a spike in anomalous API requests to our integration with Redwood late last night (2028-01-15 01:12 UTC). That traffic included unusually large payloads and a small set of keys that we don’t recognize. We're still triaging but wanted to raise an early heads-up given our DPA obligations.

At a minimum we need: 1) a preliminary notice acknowledging you received this report, 2) confirmation of the incident notification window in your DPA (our copy references "as soon as reasonably practicable and in any event within 72 hours"), and 3) a mechanism to request a forensic snapshot / logs for the affected timeframe.

We have attached a small sample of the events we saw (asteron_event_sample_logs.zip). Can you confirm who at Redwood will handle the forensic evidence request and estimated timing to get an initial scope? Also advise if any of your subprocessors are involved in routing these requests so we can loop legal.

Thanks — we appreciate a quick acknowledgement.

— Alex
Alex Gupta
Senior Security Ops
Asteron Labs
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Alex Gupta <alex.gupta@asteronlabs.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@asteronlabs.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2028-01-15T09:22:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Suspected ingestion anomaly — initial heads up

Alex — thanks for the early flag and for the sample logs. This is Kimberly on Redwood's incident & privacy team. We acknowledge receipt and will treat this as a potential security event under our DPA.

Quick answers up front:
- Acknowledgement: confirmed (this email).
- Notification window: Redwood's standard DPA incident clause reads "as soon as reasonably practicable and no later than 72 hours after becoming aware." If you have a contractual addendum referencing a shorter window, please share — otherwise we will follow the 72-hour initial notice cadence and provide a substantive update within that window.
- Forensic request: we can produce a scoped forensic snapshot (logs + KV prefixes + request metadata) subject to the DPA and mutually agreed scope. We will need you to complete the attached forensic snapshot request template so we can limit data return to least privilege.

Operational asks:
1) Please provide the narrower time window(s) you want collected (UTC) and any example request ids or API keys.
2) Indicate if you require an encrypted transfer (SFTP with customer public key preferred) and whether you need hash verification of the bundle.
3) Confirm whether you want Redwood to include any data held by subprocessors — per DPA Section 4.b, Redwood will coordinate subprocessor data access but may require additional agreements or a scoped export authorization.

We will loop in our forensics SME and subprocessor contact (cc'd) and aim to publish a preliminary scope back to you within 48 hours. If we anticipate any inability to meet the 72-hour notification (for example due to legal hold constraints), we'll escalate immediately.

— Kimberly Park
Head of Privacy & Risk, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2028-01-15T09:30:00-05:00
Subject: Fwd: Suspected ingestion anomaly — need forensic snapshot plan (Asteron)

Fyi — Alex from Asteron sent a sample and wants a preliminary notice + forensic snapshot. Key constraints / decisions we need:
- Aim for preliminary scope back within 48 hours (Kim said 48 to set expectations internally), but our DPA language is 72 hours. Recommend we target the 48-hour internal draft and finalize within 72 hours.
- Subprocessors: routing indicates requests hit our edge via CloudNet (subprocessor: cloudnet-gw). If evidence includes edge logs we need CloudNet to produce logs; coordinate with Contracts for any crossborder export.
- Transfer: prefer SFTP with customer public key; for large bundles we should use staged signed URLs from our secure bucket and provide checksums.

Action items:
Ben — can you triage the sample and produce an initial list of required artifacts? Prioritize: request headers, kv-prefixes, first 3k tokens of payloads, per-request timestamps, and raw edge logs for the time range Alex will provide.
Jordan — prep a subprocessor engagement note for CloudNet (we may need their assistance and SLA to pull edge logs). Attach the forensic_snapshot_request_template to the reply to Asteron.

I will draft the reply to Alex and mention the subprocessor involvement and likely timeline.

— Kim
From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2028-01-15T11:08:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Suspected ingestion anomaly — need forensic snapshot plan (Asteron)

On it. Quick triage of the attached sample indicates requests from two distinct API keys and an origin IP range that maps to a third-party scraping bot farm. Preliminary artifact list (will refine):
- API request headers (raw) for candidate request ids — estimated 2.4MB compressed.
- Edge gateway logs (CloudNet) for 2028-01-14 23:00 to 2028-01-15 03:00 UTC.
- per-request KV prefix snapshots (redacted PII) for affected keys — requires signed export from KV service.
- When we hand over, supply SHA256 checksums and GPG sign bundle.

Constraints/notes: CloudNet requires 24–48 hours to compile raw edge logs for export; KV exports require an export authorization ticket (legal will need to sign off). If Asteron wants subprocessor-held data included, that may push final delivery to a 7–10 day window.

I'll assemble the preliminary scope and attach the forensic template as requested.

— Ben
From: Alex Gupta <alex.gupta@asteronlabs.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@asteronlabs.com>
Date: 2028-01-18T14:22:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Suspected ingestion anomaly — initial heads up

Kimberly / Ben — thanks for the quick coordination and transparency. We completed a focused triage and can provide the following to narrow scope:
- Time ranges of interest: 2028-01-14T23:45:00Z to 2028-01-15T02:15:00Z (UTC).
- Example request ids: rq_7a4f9b, rq_7a4fcd.
- We want Redwood to include subprocessor edge logs (CloudNet) in the initial evidence bundle if feasible; otherwise please provide clear timing and escalation path.

We accept SFTP with our public key (attached in the last message) and prefer signed checksums. We also request that Redwood provide an index of potentially affected customer IDs (pseudonymized) so we can triage downstream notifications.

If export of subprocessor data will take longer, please provide an interim export limited to what Redwood controls (request headers, KV snapshots we can correlate) within the 72-hour notice window. We'll sign any required export/NDAs if needed for subprocessor-held data.

Appreciate the forensics template — we'll return it today. Please advise next steps and point person for evidence handoff.

— Alex
